## How to run

Open this file in RStudio and click **Knit**, or run its chunks from top to bottom.
The input folder is already set below. Outputs go into a new `merged_outputs_R`
subfolder; original files are never edited. Re-running replaces files in that
output subfolder. This document uses **R only**, with no Python dependency.

Install packages once in the RStudio Console if needed:

```{r install-packages, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("dplyr", "readr", "readxl", "stringr", "tibble",
                   "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
```

The merge reproduces the rules used in the previously supplied package. The main
files describe availability with **no maximum date gap**. Separate 180-day and
365-day versions require every relevant clinical/PET/blood/sleep date to be
within that window of MRI. These are alternative matching definitions, not
clinically validated cutoffs. The report does not run association analyses.

## 1. Settings and helper functions

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE)
required <- c("dplyr", "readr", "readxl", "stringr", "tibble")
missing <- required[!vapply(required, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Install these packages first: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
if (packageVersion("dplyr") < "1.1.1") stop("Please update dplyr to version 1.1.1 or newer.")
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)

data_dir <- "/Users/yueran_li/Desktop/IUSM PhD/research plans/Hypothalamic AD/Data/3003_Li_Update"
output_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "merged_outputs_R")
stopifnot(dir.exists(data_dir))
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
date_windows <- c(180, 365)

# Match a workbook by prefix; never silently take the first of several files.
find_xlsx <- function(prefix) {
  paths <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
  paths <- paths[startsWith(basename(paths), prefix)]
  if (length(paths) != 1L) stop("Expected exactly one workbook beginning '",
                              prefix, "'; found ", length(paths), ": ",
                              paste(basename(paths), collapse = ", "))
  paths
}
save_csv <- function(x, name) {
  write_csv(x, file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), na = "")
}
assert_unique <- function(x, keys, label) {
  if (anyDuplicated(as.data.frame(x[keys]))) stop("Duplicate key in ", label)
}
read_table <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(data_dir, paste0("tbl_", name, "_2026-11-03.csv"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing input: ", path)
  # Read strings first to preserve participant IDs, then convert other types.
  x <- read_csv(path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                na = c("", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  ids <- x$subid
  x <- type_convert(x, na = c("", "NA"), trim_ws = TRUE)
  x$subid <- as.character(ids)
  x$source_row <- seq_len(nrow(x)) + 1L  # header is row 1
  for (nm in names(x)[grepl("date", names(x))]) x[[nm]] <- as.Date(x[[nm]])
  x
}

# Input records must already satisfy the requested domain's completeness rules.
# Ties: smaller absolute gap, earlier date, then earlier source row.
# A measurement can be reused for several MRI scans from the same participant.
nearest_visit <- function(scans, records, date_col, prefix) {
  stopifnot(all(c("subid", date_col, "source_row") %in% names(records)))
  records <- records |> filter(!is.na(.data[[date_col]]))
  fields <- setdiff(names(records), "subid")
  rec <- records |> rename_with(~ paste0(prefix, .x), all_of(fields))
  date_name <- paste0(prefix, date_col)
  row_name <- paste0(prefix, "source_row")
  scans |> select(subject, subid, mri_date) |>
    left_join(rec, by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-many", na_matches = "never") |>
    mutate(gap_days = as.numeric(.data[[date_name]] - mri_date),
           abs_gap = abs(gap_days)) |>
    arrange(subject, abs_gap, .data[[date_name]], .data[[row_name]]) |>
    group_by(subject) |> slice_head(n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
    select(subject, all_of(paste0(prefix, fields)), gap_days) |>
    rename_with(~ paste0(prefix, "gap_days"), all_of("gap_days"))
}
```

## 2. Hypothalamus volumes and scan-level QC

The hypothalamus file contains **five subregions per hemisphere**, plus left and
right totals. We retain original volumes and add bilateral sums. Each row remains
one scan directory; multiple acquisitions on one day are not collapsed.

FS QC **Excellent** and **Good** pass; Failed or missing QC do not. Exclusions
from the supplied hypothalamus QC list apply to individual scans, not all visits
from the participant.

```{r hypothalamus-qc}
hypo_path <- find_xlsx("IADRCprisma_hypothalamic_subunits_volumes_all")
qc_path <- find_xlsx("Hypothalamus_QC_zero_and_3SD")
fs_path <- find_xlsx("IADRCNICDerivatives-PrismaDemoDxATN")
h <- read_excel(hypo_path, sheet = 1)
assert_unique(h, "subject", "hypothalamus scan directories")
volume_cols <- setdiff(names(h), "subject")
names(h)[match(volume_cols, names(h))] <- paste0(
  "hypo_", str_replace_all(volume_cols, "[ -]", "_"), "_mm3")
h <- h |> mutate(
  subid = str_match(subject, "sub-([0-9]+)")[, 2],
  mri_date = as.Date(str_match(subject, "ses-([0-9]{8})")[, 2], "%Y%m%d")
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(h$subid), !anyNA(h$mri_date))
regions <- c("anterior_inferior", "anterior_superior", "posterior",
             "tubular_inferior", "tubular_superior")
for (r in regions) {
  h[[paste0("hypo_bilateral_", r, "_mm3")]] <-
    h[[paste0("hypo_left_", r, "_mm3")]] + h[[paste0("hypo_right_", r, "_mm3")]]
}
h$hypo_total_mm3 <- h$hypo_whole_left_mm3 + h$hypo_whole_right_mm3
qc <- read_excel(qc_path, sheet = "Flagged scans")
h$hypo_flagged <- h$subject %in% qc$`Scan ID`
fs <- read_excel(fs_path, sheet = "Freesurfer") |>
  transmute(subject = `Name of Imaging Directory`, fs_qc = `FreeSurfer QC Rating`,
            fs_etiv_reference_mm3 = eTIV)
assert_unique(fs, "subject", "FreeSurfer QC")
h <- left_join(h, fs, by = "subject", relationship = "one-to-one")
count(h, fs_qc, hypo_flagged)
```

## 3. Match MRI CSV eTIV to the correct acquisition

Use participant + **exact MRI date**. When multiple MRI records occur that day,
use the QC workbook's eTIV as a reference (tolerance 0.01 mm³). The value saved as
`etiv_mm3` always comes from the November MRI CSV. Identical selected MRI fields
are collapsed for matching. Unresolved multiple candidates receive missing eTIV.

If only one distinct MRI record remains but its eTIV disagrees with the QC
workbook, retain it with `date_only_eTIV_discordant`. These scans need acquisition
confirmation before final analysis; the code also saves their audit separately.

```{r match-mri}
mri <- read_table("MRI")
mri_fields <- c("visitdate", "resolution_7", "etiv_7",
                "left_hippocampus_7", "right_hippocampus_7")
mri_matches <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(h)), function(i) {
  scan <- h[i, ]
  g <- mri |> filter(subid == scan$subid, mri_date == scan$mri_date)
  result <- tibble(subject = scan$subject, mri_candidate_rows = nrow(g),
                   mri_match_status = "no_exact_MRI_date")
  # Typed empty template also covers scans without a candidate.
  selected <- mri[NA_integer_, c(mri_fields, "source_row")]
  if (nrow(g)) {
    exact <- g |> filter(!is.na(etiv_7), !is.na(scan$fs_etiv_reference_mm3),
                         abs(etiv_7 - scan$fs_etiv_reference_mm3) <= 0.01)
    if (nrow(exact)) {
      g <- exact
      result$mri_match_status <- "date_and_FS_eTIV_concordant"
    } else result$mri_match_status <- "date_only_eTIV_discordant"
    if (nrow(distinct(g, across(all_of(mri_fields)))) == 1L) {
      selected <- g[1, c(mri_fields, "source_row")]
    } else result$mri_match_status <- "unresolved_multiple_acquisitions"
  }
  bind_cols(result, selected)
}) |> bind_rows() |>
  rename(mri_linked_visitdate = visitdate, etiv_mm3 = etiv_7,
         mri_source_row = source_row)
h <- left_join(h, mri_matches, by = "subject", relationship = "one-to-one")
```

## 4. Demographics, diagnosis, age and base inclusion

Sex and APOE come from the participant table. Genotypes 24/34/44 are ε4 positive;
22/23/33 are negative. Age at MRI is approximated from the nearest eligible
clinical visit's age plus elapsed years; original clinical age is retained.
Diagnosis categories are retained exactly, without a CN/CI recoding.

```{r base-dataset}
par <- read_table("PAR")
assert_unique(par, "subid", "participant table")
h <- h |> left_join(select(par, subid, sex, apoegenotype, educ),
                    by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(
    apoe4_status = case_when(apoegenotype %in% c(22, 23, 33) ~ 0L,
                            apoegenotype %in% c(24, 34, 44) ~ 1L,
                            TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
    apoe4_allele_count = case_when(apoegenotype %in% c(22, 23, 33) ~ 0L,
                                  apoegenotype %in% c(24, 34) ~ 1L,
                                  apoegenotype == 44 ~ 2L, TRUE ~ NA_integer_)
  )
diag <- read_table("DIAG") |>
  filter(!is.na(diagnosis), !is.na(visitage)) |>
  select(subid, visitdate, diagnosis, syndrome, subtype, contributing_cond,
         visitage, source_row)
h <- h |> left_join(nearest_visit(h, diag, "visitdate", "dx_"),
                    by = "subject", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(age_at_mri_years = dx_visitage - dx_gap_days / 365.25) |>
  group_by(subid, mri_date) |> mutate(same_day_scan_count = n()) |> ungroup()
criteria <- list(
  "All hypothalamus scans" = rep(TRUE, nrow(h)),
  "FS QC Excellent or Good" = h$fs_qc %in% c("Excellent", "Good"),
  "Unflagged hypothalamus" = !h$hypo_flagged,
  "Matched positive MRI CSV eTIV" = !is.na(h$etiv_mm3) & h$etiv_mm3 > 0,
  "Age, sex, diagnosis, APOE4 available" = !is.na(h$age_at_mri_years) &
    h$sex %in% c("F", "M") & !is.na(h$dx_diagnosis) & !is.na(h$apoe4_status)
)
keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(h))
flow <- list()
for (step in names(criteria)) {
  before <- sum(keep)
  keep <- keep & coalesce(criteria[[step]], FALSE)
  flow[[step]] <- tibble(step, scan_rows = sum(keep),
                         participants = n_distinct(h$subid[keep]),
                         excluded_at_step = before - sum(keep))
}
inclusion_flow <- bind_rows(flow)
h$included_base <- keep
base <- filter(h, included_base)
save_csv(h, "scan_inclusion_audit")
save_csv(inclusion_flow, "inclusion_flow")
save_csv(filter(base, mri_match_status != "date_and_FS_eTIV_concordant"),
         "base_MRI_matches_needing_review")
knitr::kable(inclusion_flow)
```

## 5. PET and hippocampal neurodegeneration datasets

ATNV is joined by participant + exact MRI date, preserving the data core's PET
linkage and PET measurement dates. Only positive/negative statuses qualify;
ambiguous amyloid remains in the audit. `n_hippo` is the supplied dimensionless
mean left/right hippocampal volume divided by intracranial volume. It is not
recalculated, and no new threshold is applied. On dates with multiple acquisitions,
ATNV's hippocampal ratio may refer to only one acquisition.

```{r pet-datasets}
atnv <- read_table("ATNV") |>
  rename(mri_date = mri_date_atnv, atnv_source_row = source_row) |>
  select(-any_of("threshold_date"))
assert_unique(atnv, c("subid", "mri_date"), "ATNV participant/MRI-date keys")
master <- base |> left_join(atnv, by = c("subid", "mri_date"),
                            relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(amy_date_atnv_gap_days = as.numeric(amy_date_atnv - mri_date),
         tau_date_atnv_gap_days = as.numeric(tau_date_atnv - mri_date))
definitive <- function(x) x %in% c("positive", "negative")
datasets <- list(
  "01_base" = base,
  "02_base_amyloid" = filter(master, definitive(amyloid_status)),
  "03_base_amyloid_tau" = filter(master, definitive(amyloid_status),
                                  definitive(tau_tmr_status)),
  "04_base_amyloid_tau_hippo" = filter(master, definitive(amyloid_status),
    definitive(tau_tmr_status), definitive(n_hippo_status), !is.na(n_hippo), n_hippo > 0)
)
save_csv(master, "base_ATNV_audit_including_ambiguous")
```

## 6. Compare plasma assays and select the most available pair

Only PLASMA is included. Eligible results have positive values and either no flag
or a flag explicitly saying "ok to use". Other flagged records are conservatively
excluded, even if their flag concerns a different analyte, and saved for review.
Conflicting values from the same assay/marker and collection date are excluded
rather than averaged. Identical repeat values use the latest assay date, then
latest source row. Assay versions are kept separate; platform metadata is retained.
An assay with multiple explicitly identified platforms stops for review.

Choose the Aβ/p-tau assay pair with the most **unique base participants**, requiring
both markers on the same collection date. Break ties using scan coverage, then
preference for a reported Aβ42/40 ratio. This measures availability, not clinical
superiority. The original files select Lumipulse Aβ42 plus pTau217 plus.

```{r plasma-availability}


# Keep only unflagged plasma records
blood <- read_table("BLDBIOM") |>
  filter(
    specimen_type == "PLASMA",
    is.na(flagged) | trimws(flagged) == ""
  )

# One available Aβ42/40 result per participant
ab <- blood |>
  filter(!is.na(ab4240ratio)) |>
  distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(
    subid,
    ab4240ratio,
    ab_date = procedure_date,
    ab_assay = assay_name
  )

# One available p-tau217 result per participant
tau <- blood |>
  filter(!is.na(ptau217)) |>
  distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(
    subid,
    ptau217,
    ptau_date = procedure_date,
    ptau_assay = assay_name
  )

# Match by ID; retain only participants with BOTH biomarkers
plasma <- base |>
  inner_join(ab, by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  inner_join(tau, by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-one")

datasets[["05_base_plasma"]] <- plasma

# Show final dataset
View(plasma)

# Show sample size
plasma |>
  summarise(
    subjects = n_distinct(subid),
    scans = n_distinct(subject)
  )

# Save
save_csv(plasma, "05_base_plasma_ab4240ratio_ptau217")



```

The concentration units should be confirmed with the data core before reporting
concentrations. Values are not rescaled or harmonized. The derived ratio assumes
the Aβ42 and Aβ40 concentrations share units and is an additional variable, not a
separate candidate in the availability ranking.

## 7. Complete sleep dataset

Require **all nine items from one visit**, then choose that participant's nearest
complete visit to MRI. A nearer incomplete visit can therefore be bypassed.
The updated data should contain only 0–3 codes; invalid codes stop the merge.
No PSQI global score is calculated.

```{r sleep-dataset}
sleep_raw <- read_table("SLEEP")
psq <- paste0("psq5", letters[1:9])
values <- unlist(sleep_raw[psq], use.names = FALSE)
if (any(!is.na(values) & !(values %in% 0:3))) stop("PSQI values outside 0–3; check coding before merging.")
sleep_complete <- sleep_raw |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(psq), ~ !is.na(.x))) |>
  select(subid, visitdate, source_row, all_of(psq))
sleep <- base |> left_join(nearest_visit(base, sleep_complete, "visitdate", "sleep_"),
                           by = "subject", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(paste0("sleep_", psq)), ~ !is.na(.x)))
datasets[["06_base_sleep"]] <- sleep
```

## 8. Export all datasets, date-window variants and counts

CSV files open in Excel and can be read with `read_csv()`. The RDS file preserves
R column types and holds all six main datasets in one named list.
`*_gap_days` is the measurement date minus MRI date: negative means before MRI.
Missing required dates fail the date-window filter. These filters apply to
diagnosis **as well as** the additional modality.

```{r export-and-check}
summarize_dataset <- function(x, name) {
  repeated <- x |> group_by(subid) |> summarise(n_dates = n_distinct(mri_date), .groups = "drop")
  tibble(dataset = name, scan_rows = nrow(x), participants = n_distinct(x$subid),
         distinct_MRI_dates = nrow(distinct(x, subid, mri_date)),
         participants_with_2plus_MRI_dates = sum(repeated$n_dates >= 2))
}
gap_columns <- function(name) {
  cols <- "dx_gap_days"
  if (name %in% c("02_base_amyloid", "03_base_amyloid_tau", "04_base_amyloid_tau_hippo"))
    cols <- c(cols, "amy_date_atnv_gap_days")
  if (name %in% c("03_base_amyloid_tau", "04_base_amyloid_tau_hippo"))
    cols <- c(cols, "tau_date_atnv_gap_days")
  if (name == "05_base_plasma") cols <- c(cols, "blood_gap_days")
  if (name == "06_base_sleep") cols <- c(cols, "sleep_gap_days")
  cols
}
counts <- list()
window_counts <- list()
gap_summary <- list()
for (name in names(datasets)) {
  x <- datasets[[name]]
  assert_unique(x, "subject", name)
  stopifnot(all(x$subject %in% base$subject))
  save_csv(x, name)
  counts[[name]] <- summarize_dataset(x, name)
  cols <- gap_columns(name)
  for (window in date_windows) {
    limited <- x |> filter(if_all(all_of(cols), ~ !is.na(.x) & abs(.x) <= window))
    save_csv(limited, paste0(name, "_within_", window, "d"))
    window_counts[[paste(name, window)]] <- tibble(dataset = name,
      window_days_all_modalities = window, scan_rows = nrow(limited),
      participants = n_distinct(limited$subid))
  }
  for (col in cols) {
    gaps <- abs(x[[col]]); gaps <- gaps[!is.na(gaps)]
    gap_summary[[paste(name, col)]] <- tibble(dataset = name, gap_variable = col,
      median_abs_days = if (length(gaps)) median(gaps) else NA_real_,
      max_abs_days = if (length(gaps)) max(gaps) else NA_real_)
  }
}
dataset_counts <- bind_rows(counts)
time_window_counts <- bind_rows(window_counts)
match_gap_summary <- bind_rows(gap_summary)
save_csv(dataset_counts, "dataset_counts")
save_csv(time_window_counts, "time_window_counts")
save_csv(match_gap_summary, "match_gap_summary")
saveRDS(datasets, file.path(output_dir, "IADRC_merged_datasets.rds"))

stopifnot(!any(base$hypo_flagged), all(base$fs_qc %in% c("Excellent", "Good")),
  all(datasets[["04_base_amyloid_tau_hippo"]]$subject %in% datasets[["03_base_amyloid_tau"]]$subject),
  all(datasets[["03_base_amyloid_tau"]]$subject %in% datasets[["02_base_amyloid"]]$subject))
knitr::kable(dataset_counts)
knitr::kable(time_window_counts)
knitr::kable(match_gap_summary)
```

For the original supplied files, the prior merge produced these unrestricted
counts. A mismatch here is a prompt to review source versions or merge behavior,
not a reason to force records into the expected count.

```{r compare-previous-counts}
expected <- tibble(dataset = names(datasets),
  expected_scan_rows = c(974L, 258L, 73L, 73L, 543L, 786L),
  expected_participants = c(587L, 229L, 72L, 72L, 291L, 444L))
count_check <- dataset_counts |> left_join(expected, by = "dataset") |>
  mutate(matches_previous = scan_rows == expected_scan_rows & participants == expected_participants)
save_csv(count_check, "comparison_with_previous_merge")
if (!all(count_check$matches_previous)) warning("Counts differ from the previous merge; review comparison_with_previous_merge.csv.")
knitr::kable(count_check)
cat("Output folder:", output_dir)
```

## 9. Using the results

```{r examples, eval=FALSE}
# Six main datasets are already available in the named list 'datasets'.
base <- datasets[["01_base"]]
pet_at <- datasets[["03_base_amyloid_tau"]]

# Or reload them in a new R session:
datasets <- readRDS(file.path(output_dir, "IADRC_merged_datasets.rds"))

# A time-limited dataset:
sleep_365 <- read_csv(file.path(output_dir, "06_base_sleep_within_365d.csv"))

# Optional stricter acquisition match (changes sample size):
base_concordant <- datasets[["01_base"]] |>
  filter(mri_match_status == "date_and_FS_eTIV_concordant")
```

Keep repeated MRI dates/acquisitions in mind when defining a cross-sectional or
longitudinal analysis. This merge does not choose one baseline scan per person or
average same-day acquisitions. In the prior base dataset, 30 scan rows had
discordant eTIV matches and require review. Unrestricted matches can be years
apart; review the date-gap summaries before choosing an analysis cohort.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```

```{r}



# 1. One scan per participant: earliest eligible scan
dat <- datasets[["01_base"]] |>
  arrange(subid, mri_date, subject) |>
  distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    age = age_at_mri_years,
    sex_binary = case_when(
      sex == "F" ~ 0,
      sex == "M" ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    etiv = etiv_mm3,
    dx_original = str_squish(dx_diagnosis),

    # Exclude "Impaired, not MCI" BEFORE matching other MCI labels
    dx = case_when(
      str_to_lower(dx_original) == "impaired, not mci" ~ NA_character_,
      str_detect(dx_original, regex("MCI", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "MCI",
      str_detect(dx_original, regex("^SCD", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Normal",
      str_to_lower(dx_original) == "normal" ~ "Normal",
      str_to_lower(dx_original) == "dementia" ~ "Dementia",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    dx = factor(dx, levels = c("Normal", "MCI", "Dementia"))
  )

# Show original-to-new diagnosis mapping
dat |>
  count(dx_original, dx, name = "n") |>
  print(n = Inf)

# Exclude unmapped diagnoses from diagnosis analyses only
dat_dx <- dat |>
  filter(!is.na(dx))

# Show diagnosis sample sizes
dat_dx |>
  count(dx, name = "n", .drop = FALSE) |>
  print(n = Inf)


# Bilateral volumes: left + right
regions <- c(
  "Anterior inferior" = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_inferior_mm3",
  "Anterior superior" = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_superior_mm3",
  "Posterior"         = "hypo_bilateral_posterior_mm3",
  "Tubular inferior"  = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_inferior_mm3",
  "Tubular superior"  = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_superior_mm3",
  "Total"            = "hypo_total_mm3"
)


# 2. Age, sex and three-category diagnosis analyses
results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(regions), function(region) {

  volume_col <- regions[[region]]

  # Age and sex: partial correlations controlling for eTIV
  # Uses all participants in dat, including "Impaired, not MCI"
  correlations <- bind_rows(lapply(c("age", "sex_binary"), function(pred) {

    d <- data.frame(
      volume = dat[[volume_col]],
      predictor = dat[[pred]],
      etiv = dat$etiv
    )
    d <- d[complete.cases(d), ]

    volume_resid <- residuals(lm(volume ~ etiv, data = d))
    predictor_resid <- residuals(lm(predictor ~ etiv, data = d))

    r <- cor(volume_resid, predictor_resid)

    df <- nrow(d) - 3
    t_value <- r * sqrt(df / (1 - r^2))
    p_value <- 2 * pt(abs(t_value), df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)

    tibble(
      region = region,
      predictor = ifelse(pred == "age", "Age", "Sex"),
      method = "Partial correlation controlling for eTIV",
      n = nrow(d),
      effect_type = "partial_r",
      effect = r,
      statistic = t_value,
      df1 = 1,
      df2 = df,
      p = p_value
    )
  }))

  # Diagnosis: Normal, MCI and Dementia only
  d <- data.frame(
    volume = dat_dx[[volume_col]],
    dx = dat_dx$dx,
    etiv = dat_dx$etiv
  )
  d <- d[complete.cases(d), ]
  d$dx <- droplevels(d$dx)

  reduced <- lm(volume ~ etiv, data = d)
  full <- lm(volume ~ etiv + dx, data = d)

  # Omnibus diagnosis effect after accounting for eTIV
  comparison <- anova(reduced, full)

  partial_eta2 <- (
    deviance(reduced) - deviance(full)
  ) / deviance(reduced)

  diagnosis <- tibble(
    region = region,
    predictor = "Diagnosis",
    method = "ANCOVA adjusting for eTIV",
    n = nrow(d),
    effect_type = "partial_eta_squared",
    effect = partial_eta2,
    statistic = comparison$F[2],
    df1 = comparison$Df[2],
    df2 = df.residual(full),
    p = comparison$`Pr(>F)`[2]
  )

  bind_rows(correlations, diagnosis)
}))


# 3. FDR across all 18 tests
results <- results |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

results |>
  mutate(across(c(effect, statistic, p, p_fdr), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)


# 4. Whole-hypothalamus differences compared with Normal
whole_dat <- dat_dx |>
  filter(
    !is.na(hypo_total_mm3),
    !is.na(etiv)
  )

# Ensure all three groups are present
stopifnot(
  all(c("Normal", "MCI", "Dementia") %in% as.character(whole_dat$dx))
)

# Explicitly use Normal as the reference group
whole_dat$dx <- factor(
  whole_dat$dx,
  levels = c("Normal", "MCI", "Dementia")
)
contrasts(whole_dat$dx) <- contr.treatment(
  levels(whole_dat$dx),
  base = 1
)

whole_fit <- lm(
  hypo_total_mm3 ~ etiv + dx,
  data = whole_dat
)

coef_table <- summary(whole_fit)$coefficients
ci <- confint(whole_fit, level = 0.95)

terms <- c("dxMCI", "dxDementia")

whole_contrasts <- tibble(
  comparison = c("MCI vs Normal", "Dementia vs Normal"),
  n_normal = sum(whole_dat$dx == "Normal"),
  n_comparison = c(
    sum(whole_dat$dx == "MCI"),
    sum(whole_dat$dx == "Dementia")
  ),
  n_model = nrow(whole_dat),
  difference_mm3 = unname(coef_table[terms, "Estimate"]),
  SE = unname(coef_table[terms, "Std. Error"]),
  CI_lower = unname(ci[terms, 1]),
  CI_upper = unname(ci[terms, 2]),
  p = unname(coef_table[terms, "Pr(>|t|)"])
) |>
  mutate(
    # Separate FDR family for these two additional contrasts
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

whole_contrasts |>
  mutate(
    across(c(difference_mm3, SE, CI_lower, CI_upper), ~ round(.x, 2)),
    across(c(p, p_fdr), ~ signif(.x, 4))
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)


# 5. Save results
write.csv(
  results,
  file.path(output_dir, "hypothalamus_age_sex_dx3_adjusted_eTIV_FDR.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  whole_contrasts,
  file.path(output_dir, "whole_hypothalamus_MCI_Dementia_vs_Normal.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
# 1. Keep the earliest eligible MRI for each participant
earliest_scan <- function(data) {
  data |>
    arrange(subid, mri_date, subject) |>
    distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

base_dat   <- earliest_scan(datasets[["01_base"]])
plasma_dat <- earliest_scan(datasets[["05_base_plasma"]])

# 2. Bilateral subregion volumes and whole hypothalamus volume (mm³)
regions <- c(
  "Anterior inferior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_inferior_mm3",
  "Anterior superior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_superior_mm3",
  "Posterior"          = "hypo_bilateral_posterior_mm3",
  "Tubular inferior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_inferior_mm3",
  "Tubular superior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_superior_mm3",
  "Whole hypothalamus" = "hypo_total_mm3"
)

# 3. Test one predictor across all six volumes, adjusting for eTIV
test_predictor <- function(data, predictor_col, label) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(regions), function(region) {

    formula <- reformulate(
      c("etiv_mm3", predictor_col),
      response = regions[[region]]
    )
    fit <- lm(formula, data = data, na.action = na.omit)

    term <- coef(summary(fit))[predictor_col, ]
    t_value <- unname(term["t value"])
    df <- df.residual(fit)

    tibble(
      region    = region,
      predictor = label,
      n         = nobs(fit),
      B_mm3     = unname(term["Estimate"]),
      partial_r = t_value / sqrt(t_value^2 + df),
      p         = unname(term["Pr(>|t|)"])
    )
  }))
}

# 4. Combine all 18 tests and apply FDR correction once
results_etiv <- bind_rows(
  test_predictor(base_dat,   "apoe4_status", "APOE ε4 carrier"),
  test_predictor(plasma_dat, "ab4240ratio",  "Plasma Aβ42/40"),
  test_predictor(plasma_dat, "ptau217",      "Plasma p-tau217")
) |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

print(results_etiv, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)



# All QC-eligible base MRIs are candidates, including follow-up MRIs.
mri_pool <- datasets[["01_base"]] |>
  mutate(mri_date = as.Date(mri_date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(subid), !is.na(mri_date))

closest_mri_to_pet <- function(pet_date_col, status_col) {

  # Use the actual PET acquisition date from ATNV.
  # Collapse repeated references to the same participant/PET date/status.
  pet_visits <- atnv |>
    transmute(
      subid,
      pet_date = as.Date(.data[[pet_date_col]]),
      pet_status = tolower(trimws(as.character(.data[[status_col]])))
    ) |>
    filter(
      !is.na(subid), !is.na(pet_date),
      pet_status %in% c("negative", "positive")
    ) |>
    distinct()

  # Avoid assigning an arbitrary status if the same PET date has both labels.
  if (anyDuplicated(pet_visits[c("subid", "pet_date")]) > 0L) {
    stop("Conflicting ", status_col, " values for the same participant and PET date.")
  }

  mri_pool |>
    inner_join(pet_visits, by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(
      mri_minus_pet_days = as.integer(mri_date - pet_date),
      abs_gap_days = abs(mri_minus_pet_days),
      pet_positive = as.integer(pet_status == "positive")
    ) |>
    # For equal gaps, prefer the earlier MRI, then the earlier PET.
    # subject breaks any remaining tie between same-day MRI scans.
    arrange(subid, abs_gap_days, mri_date, pet_date, subject) |>
    distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

pet_data <- list(
  "Amyloid PET" = closest_mri_to_pet("amy_date_atnv", "amyloid_status"),
  "Tau PET"     = closest_mri_to_pet("tau_date_atnv", "tau_tmr_status")
)

# Verify one MRI per participant and summarize how far apart the visits were.
pet_counts <- imap_dfr(pet_data, function(d, marker) {
  stopifnot(nrow(d) == n_distinct(d$subid))

  tibble(
    marker = marker,
    participants = n_distinct(d$subid),
    mri_scans = nrow(d),
    pet_negative = sum(d$pet_positive == 0),
    pet_positive = sum(d$pet_positive == 1),
    median_gap_days = median(d$abs_gap_days),
    within_1_year = sum(d$abs_gap_days <= 365),
    over_1_year = sum(d$abs_gap_days > 365)
  )
})

print(pet_counts, width = Inf)
```

```{r}
pet_results <- imap_dfr(pet_data, function(cohort, marker) {
  imap_dfr(regions, function(volume_col, region_label) {

    d <- cohort |>
      transmute(subid, volume = .data[[volume_col]], etiv_mm3, pet_positive) |>
      filter(is.finite(volume), is.finite(etiv_mm3))

    if (n_distinct(d$pet_positive) < 2) {
      stop("Both PET groups are required for ", marker, " / ", region_label)
    }

    fit <- lm(volume ~ etiv_mm3 + pet_positive, data = d)

    # Participant-clustered standard errors for repeated MRI scans
    test <- clubSandwich::coef_test(
      fit, vcov = "CR2", cluster = d$subid, test = "Satterthwaite"
    )
    pet <- test[match("pet_positive", names(coef(fit))), ]
    margin <- qt(0.975, df = pet$df_Satt) * pet$SE

    tibble(
      marker = marker,
      region = region_label,
      participants = n_distinct(d$subid),
      mri_scans = nrow(d),
      difference_mm3 = pet$beta,
      ci_low_mm3 = pet$beta - margin,
      ci_high_mm3 = pet$beta + margin,
      p = pet$p_Satt
    )
  })
}) |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),  # 2 PET markers × 6 volumes
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

pet_results |>
  mutate(across(c(difference_mm3, ci_low_mm3, ci_high_mm3, p, p_fdr),
                ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)

write.csv(pet_counts, file.path(output_dir, "hypothalamus_PET_counts.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pet_results, file.path(output_dir, "hypothalamus_PET_eTIV_FDR.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)

regions <- c(
  "Anterior inferior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_inferior_mm3",
  "Anterior superior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_superior_mm3",
  "Posterior"          = "hypo_bilateral_posterior_mm3",
  "Tubular inferior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_inferior_mm3",
  "Tubular superior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_superior_mm3",
  "Whole hypothalamus" = "hypo_total_mm3"
)

# The increment sets the scale of the reported coefficient.
pet_specs <- tribble(
  ~predictor,         ~date_col,       ~value_col,       ~binary, ~increment,
  "Amyloid status",   "amy_date_atnv", "amyloid_status", TRUE,     1,
  "Amyloid Centiloid","amy_date_atnv", "a_centiloid",    FALSE,   10,
  "Tau status",       "tau_date_atnv", "tau_tmr_status", TRUE,     1,
  "Tau TMR",          "tau_date_atnv", "t_tmr",          FALSE,    0.1
)

mri_pool <- datasets[["01_base"]] |>
  select(subid, subject, mri_date, etiv_mm3, all_of(unname(regions))) |>
  mutate(mri_date = as.Date(mri_date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(subid), !is.na(mri_date), is.finite(etiv_mm3))

# 1. Select the closest eligible MRI–PET pair for each person and predictor.
match_pet <- function(predictor, date_col, value_col, binary, increment) {
  raw <- trimws(as.character(atnv[[value_col]]))

  if (binary) {
    value <- case_when(
      tolower(raw) == "positive" ~ 1,
      tolower(raw) == "negative" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  } else {
    value <- as.numeric(raw)
  }

  visits <- tibble(
    subid = atnv$subid,
    pet_date = as.Date(atnv[[date_col]]),
    pet_value = value
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(subid), !is.na(pet_date), is.finite(pet_value)) |>
    distinct()

  # Repeated ATNV rows for one PET visit are fine if their values agree.
  if (anyDuplicated(visits[c("subid", "pet_date")]) > 0L) {
    stop("Conflicting ", value_col, " values for the same participant and PET date.")
  }

  mri_pool |>
    inner_join(visits, by = "subid", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    mutate(gap_days = abs(as.integer(mri_date - pet_date))) |>
    arrange(subid, gap_days, mri_date, pet_date, subject) |>
    distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    mutate(predictor = .env$predictor, x = pet_value / increment)
}

pet_matched <- pmap(pet_specs, match_pet) |> bind_rows()

# Show the actual sample size and MRI–PET separation for each predictor.
pet_counts <- pet_matched |>
  group_by(predictor) |>
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(subid),
    mri_scans = n(),
    median_gap_days = median(gap_days),
    over_365_days = sum(gap_days > 365),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(pet_counts)

# 2. Fit each region separately: volume ~ PET predictor + eTIV.
fit_regions <- function(cohort) {
  imap_dfr(regions, function(volume_col, region_name) {
    d <- cohort |>
      transmute(volume = .data[[volume_col]], x, etiv_mm3) |>
      filter(is.finite(volume))

    fit <- lm(volume ~ x + etiv_mm3, data = d)
    coef_x <- coef(summary(fit))["x", ]
    ci <- confint(fit, parm = "x")
    t_value <- unname(coef_x["t value"])

    tibble(
      region = region_name,
      n = nrow(d),
      B_mm3 = unname(coef_x["Estimate"]),
      ci_low = ci[1, 1],
      ci_high = ci[1, 2],
      partial_r = t_value / sqrt(t_value^2 + df.residual(fit)),
      p = unname(coef_x["Pr(>|t|)"])
    )
  })
}

pet_results <- pet_matched |>
  group_by(predictor) |>
  group_modify(~ fit_regions(.x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),  # all 4 predictors × 6 volumes
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

pet_results |>
  mutate(across(c(B_mm3, ci_low, ci_high, partial_r, p, p_fdr),
                ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)

write.csv(pet_results,
          file.path(output_dir, "hypothalamus_PET_status_and_continuous_eTIV.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}


# Modified PSQI sleep-disturbance outcome using 5b–5i.
# Eight items scored 0–3 give a total of 0–24.
# Apply the raw-score cutoff corresponding to Laurell's component score ≥2:
# 0–9 = lower disturbance; 10–24 = higher disturbance.
# Because 5j is unavailable, this approximates the published outcome.
items <- paste0("sleep_psq5", letters[2:9])

regions <- c(
  "Anterior inferior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_inferior_mm3",
  "Anterior superior"  = "hypo_bilateral_anterior_superior_mm3",
  "Posterior"          = "hypo_bilateral_posterior_mm3",
  "Tubular inferior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_inferior_mm3",
  "Tubular superior"   = "hypo_bilateral_tubular_superior_mm3",
  "Whole hypothalamus" = "hypo_total_mm3"
)

sleep <- datasets[["06_base_sleep"]]

# Use the harmonized 0–3 item scores. Flag unexpected codes before scoring.
stopifnot(all(vapply(
  sleep[items],
  function(x) all(is.na(x) | x %in% 0:3),
  logical(1)
)))

# Among the available MRI–sleep pairs, keep the closest pair per participant.
# No time restriction. For equal gaps, prefer the earlier MRI.
dat <- sleep |>
  filter(
    !is.na(subid), !is.na(sleep_gap_days),
    if_all(all_of(items), ~ !is.na(.x)),
    is.finite(age_at_mri_years), !is.na(sex), is.finite(etiv_mm3)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(all_of(items), ~ as.integer(as.character(.x))),
    disturbance_sum = rowSums(pick(all_of(items))),
    high_disturbance = as.integer(disturbance_sum >= 10),
    sex = factor(sex)
  ) |>
  arrange(subid, abs(sleep_gap_days), mri_date, sleep_visitdate, subject) |>
  distinct(subid, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Check sample size, outcome balance, and MRI–sleep timing.
dat |>
  summarise(
    participants = n(),
    lower_disturbance = sum(high_disturbance == 0),
    higher_disturbance = sum(high_disturbance == 1),
    median_gap_days = median(abs(sleep_gap_days))
  ) |>
  print()

# Six logistic regressions, one per volume.
# Scale volume so OR > 1 means higher odds of disturbance per 1 SD SMALLER volume.
results <- imap_dfr(regions, function(volume_col, region_name) {
  d <- dat |>
    filter(is.finite(.data[[volume_col]])) |>
    mutate(smaller_volume_sd = -as.numeric(scale(.data[[volume_col]])))

  fit <- glm(
    high_disturbance ~ smaller_volume_sd + age_at_mri_years + sex + etiv_mm3,
    data = d,
    family = binomial()
  )

  term <- coef(summary(fit))["smaller_volume_sd", ]
  b  <- unname(term["Estimate"])
  se <- unname(term["Std. Error"])

  tibble(
    region = region_name,
    n = nrow(d),
    n_higher_disturbance = sum(d$high_disturbance),
    OR_per_SD_smaller = exp(b),
    CI_low = exp(b - 1.96 * se),
    CI_high = exp(b + 1.96 * se),
    p = unname(term["Pr(>|z|)"])
  )
}) |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    significant_fdr = p_fdr < 0.05
  )

results |>
  mutate(across(c(OR_per_SD_smaller, CI_low, CI_high, p, p_fdr),
                ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)

write.csv(
  results,
  file.path(output_dir, "hypothalamus_PSQI_5b_5i_disturbance.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
